lockState.searchScope: the full recursive git tree at the pinned revision (208 blobs)
lockState.consequence: The dependency closure IS pinned by the repository. Unlike the unlocked React fixtures in this corpus, a baseline install here reproduces the 2021 closure rather than resolving ranges against today's registry. This is the strongest reproducibility position of any React fixture ingested so far.

declaredDependencies.rangeStyle: every direct dependency and devDependency is an exact version with no range operator

resolutionsField.honoured: yarn 1 honoured all three; it emitted incompatibility warnings for @babel/compat-data against five requested ranges and applied the resolution anyway.

installedClosure.frozenLockfileMeaning: yarn verified that the committed yarn.lock already satisfies package.json exactly and refused to update it. The install therefore reproduces the committed closure and did not drift.
installedClosure.lifecycleScriptsSkippedNote: postinstall (husky install) and any dependency install scripts were not run. No native module was compiled; the closure needs none for install, typecheck or build.

warnings.character: All warnings are pre-existing properties of the 2021 closure (react-infinite-calendar and react-virtualized declaring React 15/16 peers against React 17, @percy/cypress declaring a Cypress 3-6 peer against Cypress 8). None blocked the install, the typecheck or the build.

nonclaims: A reproducible install is not a reproducible build environment: the closure is pinned but the Node runtime, the operating system and the CPU architecture are not pinned by the repository beyond .nvmrc and engines.
This record evaluates no dependency's licence, security posture, or maintenance status.
